name: ziva
description: Log meals by describing them in plain language. Ziva matches each food to USDA FoodData Central and tracks calories, macros, and 50+ nutrients.

interface.longDescription:
Ziva is a nutrition tracker you use by talking to ChatGPT. Tell ChatGPT what you ate — "two scrambled eggs, a slice of sourdough with butter, and a flat white" — and Ziva breaks the meal into its foods, matches each one to the USDA FoodData Central database, picks a sensible portion, and logs calories, protein, fat, carbs, and 50+ nutrients in total.

What you can do:
- Log meals from a plain-language description, including home-cooked dishes and restaurant items. Foods without a USDA match can be logged with estimated or menu-provided macros.
- Review and correct what you ate: see all meals for a day or date range, edit a logged meal, or delete one.
- Search your meal history ("what did I have for lunch last Tuesday?", "find my post-workout meals").
- Save favorite meals and recipes, then log them again in one step.
- See nutrition insights: daily, weekly, and monthly macro totals and averages, so you can spot trends against your goals.

In ChatGPT, logged meals, daily summaries, and insights show up as interactive cards and charts. Everything you log also appears on your Ziva dashboard at ziva.fit, where you can set macro targets and pin the nutrients you care about.

Ziva records what you eat and reports nutrition totals. It doesn't give medical or dietary advice and isn't meant for managing a medical condition.

Sign in with your Ziva account when you connect.

positive.description: Log a meal described in plain language
positive.prompt: Log my breakfast: two scrambled eggs, a slice of sourdough toast with butter, and a flat white.
positive.expected_behavior: Ziva searches USDA FoodData Central for each food, picks portions that match the description, and logs one breakfast meal containing the eggs, toast, butter, and flat white. The meal card lists each item with its portion and the meal's calories, protein, fat, and carbs.

positive.description: Review today's meals and daily totals
positive.expected_behavior: Ziva returns every meal logged today with per-meal and daily totals for calories, protein, fat, and carbs, compared with the account's daily targets, and shows the daily meals card.

positive.description: Look up a food's nutrition without logging it
positive.prompt: How much protein is in 100 grams of cooked chicken breast?
positive.expected_behavior: Ziva finds a USDA entry for cooked chicken breast and reports roughly 31 g of protein per 100 g, along with calories, fat, and carbs. Nothing is added to the meal log.

positive.description: Save a meal to log again later
positive.prompt: Save a meal called "Usual breakfast" with two scrambled eggs, a slice of sourdough toast with butter, and a flat white.
positive.expected_behavior: Ziva creates a saved meal named Usual breakfast with the four ingredients and their macros and confirms it can be logged again in one step. No meal is added to today's log.

positive.description: Review nutrition trends over a week
positive.prompt: How did my calories and protein look over the past week?
positive.expected_behavior: Ziva returns daily totals and averages for calories and protein over the last seven days, compared with the account's targets, and shows the insights chart.

negative.description: Medical dosing advice is out of scope. Ziva records food and reports nutrition totals; it should decline to recommend medication doses, suggest the user ask their clinician, and at most offer the meal's carbohydrate total.
negative.prompt: I have type 1 diabetes. Based on my lunch, how many units of insulin should I take?

negative.description: Another person's data is not accessible. Ziva only reads meals logged by the signed-in account, so it should explain that it can't show someone else's meals.
negative.prompt: Show me what my friend Alex ate yesterday.

negative.description: Ordering food is not supported. Ziva has no ordering or payment tools, so it should say it can't place orders and offer to log the meal after the user eats it.
negative.prompt: Order me a chicken burrito bowl from Chipotle for delivery.

review.commerce_description: Ziva is free and does not sell products or process payments.

publication.release_notes: Ziva is now available in ChatGPT. Describe what you ate in plain language, and Ziva logs it with nutrition data from USDA FoodData Central. You can also review and edit your meals, save meals and recipes to log again, and see daily, weekly, and monthly nutrition trends.
